headline: Native Flowers Prove Powerful Pollinator Solution
meta_description: Two-year study of 18 Ohio farms reveals native flower planting is the most effective pollinator conservation strategy.
summary_short: A two-year study across 18 Ohio farms found that planting native flowers outperforms other conservation methods for protecting pollinators.
body:
A two-year study of 18 Ohio farms has identified the single most effective strategy for protecting pollinators: planting native flowers.

The research shows that native flowers work best when paired with a few other simple habits, though the specifics of those companion practices remain part of the larger study. The findings underscore how accessible pollinator conservation can be—farmers don't need complex interventions, just the right plants native to their region.

Pollinators face mounting pressures from habitat loss and agricultural practices. This study offers practical hope: the solution often grows right where farmers live. By choosing native species, farms can rebuild the ecosystems that support bees, butterflies, and other essential pollinators while maintaining productive operations.
quick_facts: Native flower planting proved most effective strategy
Works better when paired with simple additional habits
Focuses on native species for regional ecosystems
